Use general medicinal-chemistry knowledge to interpret structures, but ground
every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not

claims.claim: Fed-state human absolute bioavailability for structurally related fluorobenzyl/azole drugs is high: rufinamide ~85% and safinamide 95.3%, supporting F >= 20% for the query's fluorobenzyl azaindazole motif under fed conditions.

Dabrafenib, which shares a 2-aminopyrimidine and aryl-fluoride/heteroaromatic framework with the query, has absolute oral bioavailability of 95%, indicating this chemotype can be well absorbed orally.
Alfuzosin, an aminopyrimidine/quinazoline-type drug, has F = 49% under fed conditions, still well above the 20% threshold.
All L1 gold records report F values from approximately 49% to 95%; none provide affirmative evidence for F < 20%.

No L2 records yet; additional source-domain context is not available.
Query-specific solubility, permeability, and first-pass data are absent; physicochemical priors are mixed (TPSA 146.9, HBA 9, low Fsp3).
Food-effect magnitude for the query is unknown; fed-state transfer from analogs is inferred rather than measured.
Structural differences from the training drugs (larger MW, higher polarity, more H-bond acceptors) may reduce transferability.
